text: {"observations":"No pitched content: f0 salience stays at 3-6% throughout, so there are no voices, horns or engine tones, and no speech-like modulation. The sound is broadband with energy weighted to the lows (centroid about 322 Hz) and falls smoothly towards 8 kHz. Loudness rises and falls in slow, regular swells peaking at about 0-1 s, 7.5-9 s, 15-16 s and again from 22 s, roughly every 7.4 s, with quiet lulls in between (3-5 s, 11-12 s, 18-20 s) during which the upper bands drop away. Onsets cluster only inside these swells. This regular surge-and-recede pattern fits waves breaking and washing on a shore, pointing to C. It argues against A and B, which would show voices, tonal events and irregular transients, and against D, since wind gusts would be irregular rather than evenly spaced.","answer":"C"}
